name: Arbitrage contract 0x6883fe4d pays any Uniswap V2 pair that calls uniswapV2Call
summary: The unverified arbitrage contract's uniswapV2Call (0x10d1e85c) accepts any pair created by a registered factory, so a pair the attacker creates on the spot passes, and then it swaps through a pair named in the callback data and transfers the owed token to the calling pair from its own balance, without checking that it started the swap. Inside a DAI/WETH flash swap, the attacker's contract created a fake token, a genuine Uniswap V2 pair of it with WETH, and a fake second pair, and swapped on its pair with data that made the pair call the contract back; the contract paid the pair 0.269 WETH, which the attacker then swapped out. Copycats used the same callback for 139.90 USDC, 30.73 USDT, 0.00041 WBTC and 0.00041 WETH.
notes: Mechanism from traces, as the contract is unverified: the exploit's callback comes from 0x986a80de, a real Uniswap V2 pair the attacker created in the same transaction for its fake token and WETH; the only storage the contract reads in the exploit is its registered-factory slot, consistent with a CREATE2 pair check that any new pair of that factory passes. The contract then calls the attacker's fake pair 0x25bcc6f7 and transfers 0.269 WETH to 0x986a80de.

Reset is the owner's 0x164b34e9(0, UniswapV2Factory) (block 15545578), which registered the factory whose pairs the callback accepts; the contract was deployed two days earlier (0x5c20ac16), and resets.mjs shows no other change before the anchor.

Every token movement of the contract since deployment (Etherscan tokentx, 49 transfers) was grouped by transaction: before the anchor it only gained from its operator 0x99d2e419's nine arbitrages, so the anchor is the first exploit; the four later losses are uniswapV2Call calls from attacker-created pairs (0x9943f268 three times in the next hours, 0x3e4033d1 in October 2026).
Loss is the contract's token outflow in the five transactions, priced by loss.mjs.
